fieldMarks: Body length 80-130 cm, over half of it tail
Grayish-brown coat with silver grizzling; long pointed flexible snout
White band near the snout tip, white spots above and below each eye and on each cheek
Long tapering tail with black rings, held erect when walking
Black feet, forefeet with bent claws
behavior: Primarily diurnal, some night activity; most active in morning and evening
Omnivorous; prefers fruit and berries; forages on the ground and in trees
Groups of a dozen or more (mothers and young) travel together; males are solitary most of the year
habitat: Broken tropical forest, pine forest, mesquite grassland and oak scrub; in the southwestern US, canyons, usually near water.
range: Central Arizona, southwestern New Mexico and southern Texas south through Mexico and Central America; occurrences farther north in Arizona/New Mexico likely wanderers or released captives. Texas status uncertain.

lookalikes.name: Ringtail
lookalikes.howToTell: Much smaller, cat-like, with a short muzzle and a black-and-white ringed tail.
